# Images

**Foundation group:** visual elements  
**Reviewed against:** GOV.UK Frontend 6.5.0 on 2026-09-09

Use images only for a demonstrated user need and ensure their information remains available to people who cannot see them.

## Rules

- Begin with clear written content and add an image only when research shows that it helps users understand or complete the service.
- Treat an image as a visual aid; all information needed to complete the task must also exist in text or another accessible form.
- Use photography, illustration and icons consistently and avoid decorative stock imagery.
- Avoid images containing text because the text cannot reflow, translate or respond reliably to user settings.
- Supply intrinsic width and height and responsive sizing to reduce layout shifts without cropping essential information.

## Accessibility contract

- Write concise alt text that communicates the image's purpose in context; use an empty alt attribute for a genuinely decorative image.
- Do not repeat nearby visible text in alt text or begin it with image of.
- For complex diagrams, provide the equivalent information in adjacent text or a linked accessible description.
- Maintain sufficient contrast for meaningful details and do not communicate distinctions by colour alone.

## Restrictions and caveats

- Do not copy or redistribute GOV.UK crowns, logotypes, favicons or other identity assets from this repository; obtain approved assets through official GOV.UK Frontend channels when the service is eligible.
- Do not replace a native control or a text label with an unexplained icon.

## Token references

No portable token is appropriate for this guidance.

## Examples

### Informative responsive image

```html
<img src="/assets/permit-example.webp" alt="Permit number highlighted in the top-right corner" width="800" height="450" style="max-width: 100%; height: auto">
```
